config.name: Everest Three Passes from Jiri
config.description: The old approach walk from the road head at Jiri over the Lamjura La and through Solu to the Dudh Koshi, joined to the Everest Three Passes circuit and walked anticlockwise for acclimatisation: up the Bhote Koshi past Thame, over the Renjo La to Gokyo, across the Ngozumpa glacier and over the Cho La, up the Khumbu to Gorak Shep (walked out and back from Lobuche, for Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar), over the Kongma La to Chhukhung, and down the Imja valley past Tengboche and Namche to Lukla. Every village has lodges with meals and a bed; Jiri, Namche and Lukla are the only real shops. Alternatives: the Gokyo valley via Machhermo instead of Thame and the Renjo La, the Khunde high route from Namche to Thame, and the north-side return from Pangboche through Phortse. Hikers flying in start at Lukla, an hour above Chheplung. Glacier crossings move from year to year: follow the current cairns.

dataSource.text: Tracks routed over the OpenStreetMap footpath network and waypoints resolved to OpenStreetMap places, peaks and saddles (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL). Elevation from SRTM 1-arcsec (NASA, public domain).

knownRetraces.note: Lobuche to Gorak Shep and back, for Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar; the detector merges it with the walk back down the Dudh Koshi from Namche to Chheplung, which retraces the walk up

waypoints.name: Jiri
waypoints.description: 1,905 m. Road head, 8-10 hr bus or jeep from Kathmandu. 10+ lodges, shops, bank and an airstrip. Last easy full resupply until Namche. Gaurishankar Conservation Area permit is issued from here.

waypoints.name: Shivalaya
waypoints.description: 1,767 m. Around six lodges by the bridge over the Khimti Khola. The road now reaches here, so many trekkers start from Shivalaya and skip the Jiri day. Permit check post.

waypoints.name: Deurali
waypoints.description: 2,705 m. Small pass with 3-4 simple lodges right on the crest, plus a viewpoint. Cold and exposed but a good short first day from Shivalaya. The Thodung yak-cheese factory is about 2 hr north.

waypoints.name: Bhandar
waypoints.description: ~2,100 m (often quoted as 2,190 m). Sherpa village below Deurali with a gompa, chortens and around five lodges. The usual first or second night out of Jiri. Mapped in OSM as Tallo (Lower) Bhandar.

waypoints.name: Kinja
waypoints.description: 1,634 m. Three or four lodges on the Likhu Khola. Hot and low; normally a lunch stop rather than a night. The 950 m climb to Sete starts immediately after the bridge.

waypoints.name: Sete
waypoints.description: 2,595 m. Three or four basic lodges on the ridge above Kinja. Standard stop after the big climb. Water can be short late in the dry season.

waypoints.name: Dakchu
waypoints.description: ~2,860 m. One or two teahouses. Useful if you want to shorten the Lamjura La day. Spelled Dagchu on some maps.

waypoints.name: Lamjura La
waypoints.description: 3,530 m. Highest point between Jiri and Namche, through rhododendron and fir forest. There is a viewpoint and a small restaurant right on the pass. Snow is possible from December to March.

waypoints.name: Junbesi
waypoints.description: ~2,675 m. Pretty Sherpa village with a large gompa and the best lodges between Jiri and Lukla. Good rest-day base; Thubten Choling monastery is about 1.5 hr up the valley.

waypoints.name: Ringmu
waypoints.description: 2,785 m. Small village with 2-3 lodges and apple orchards, just below the climb to Taksindu La. Also spelled Ringmo.

waypoints.name: Taksindu La
waypoints.description: 3,071 m. Forested pass with a mani wall and the first clear view east towards the Dudh Koshi. Also written Trakshindu La.

waypoints.name: Taksindu
waypoints.description: 2,925 m. Two or three lodges just below the pass, beside Taksindu monastery. A quieter alternative to pushing on to Nunthala.

waypoints.name: Nunthala
waypoints.description: 2,220 m. Half a dozen lodges; the standard night after the Taksindu La. Also called Manidingma.

waypoints.name: Jubing
waypoints.description: 1,680 m. Rai village on the Dudh Koshi with a couple of lodges. Low, warm and often the hottest point of the approach walk.

waypoints.name: Kharikhola
waypoints.description: 2,035 m. Strung-out village with several lodges, shops and a monastery. A common night between Nunthala and Bupsa.

waypoints.name: Bupsa
waypoints.description: 2,350 m. Three or four lodges on the hillside above Kharikhola. Bakery, and the last easy water for a while on the climb to Khari La.

waypoints.name: Kharte
waypoints.description: 2,565 m. Handful of teahouses on the climb from Bupsa - a useful break before the Khari La.

waypoints.name: Khari La
waypoints.description: 3,080 m. High point of the Bupsa-Puiya section, with views north into the Dudh Koshi gorge.

waypoints.name: Puiya
waypoints.description: ~2,775 m. Two or three lodges in a steep side valley. Also spelled Puiyan or Paiya. Landslide-prone trail on both sides.

waypoints.name: Chutok La
waypoints.description: 2,775 m. Small pass above Puiya; the trail then contours down to Surke.

waypoints.name: Surke
waypoints.description: 2,300 m. Three or four lodges. Junction: left climbs steeply to Lukla, straight on stays low and joins the main trail at Chheplung.

waypoints.name: Chaurikharka
waypoints.description: ~2,665 m. Village on the low trail between Surke and Chheplung, bypassing the climb to Lukla. Lodges, school and a gompa.

waypoints.name: Chheplung
waypoints.description: 2,660 m. Where the Jiri and Lukla trails merge. Several lodges; mapped in OSM as Cheplung.

waypoints.name: Ghat
waypoints.description: ~2,530 m. Also Nurning Ghat. Small village with lodges, a gompa and carved mani stones beside the Dudh Koshi.

waypoints.name: Phakding
waypoints.description: 2,610 m. Large lodge village on both banks of the Dudh Koshi; the standard first night out of Lukla.

waypoints.name: Monjo
waypoints.description: 2,835 m. Sagarmatha National Park entrance is just beyond the village - permits and TIMS checked here. Good lodges.

waypoints.name: Jorsalle
waypoints.description: ~2,795 m. Last lodges and last shop before the 600 m climb to Namche. The trail crosses the Hillary Bridge shortly after.

waypoints.name: Namche Bazaar
waypoints.description: 3,440 m. The Khumbu's main town: banks, ATMs, bakeries, gear shops, hospital, wifi. Saturday market. Plan two nights here to acclimatise.

waypoints.name: Thamo
waypoints.description: ~3,440 m. Quiet village on the Bhote Koshi with a few lodges and the Khari Gompa nunnery just above.

waypoints.name: Thame
waypoints.description: 3,820 m. Home village of Tenzing Norgay and many Everest summiters. Several lodges. The gompa on the hillside is well worth the climb. Damaged by a glacial-lake outburst flood in August 2024 - check current lodge availability before relying on it.

waypoints.name: Marulung
waypoints.description: ~4,210 m. Two lodges in a summer-pasture settlement on the Bhote Koshi. Also spelled Marlung.

waypoints.name: Lungden
waypoints.description: 4,380 m. Last settlement before the Renjo La - two or three lodges. Mapped in OSM as Langden. Leave very early for the pass.

waypoints.name: Relama Tsho
waypoints.description: ~4,900 m. Tarn in the upper valley, passed close on the left about two thirds of the way up to the Renjo La. Reliable landmark in poor visibility. Unnamed in OSM.

waypoints.name: Renjo La
waypoints.description: 5,398 m by OSM/SRTM; guidebooks quote anything from 5,360 to 5,420 m. First of the three passes. Stone staircase on the east side down to Gokyo, with the classic view of Everest, Lhotse and Makalu over the Gokyo lakes.

waypoints.name: Gokyo
waypoints.description: 4,750 m. Lodge settlement on the shore of Dudh Pokhari (third Gokyo lake), under the Ngozumpa glacier. Bakery, several good lodges. Standard acclimatisation stop.

waypoints.name: Thagnak
waypoints.description: 4,700 m. Two or three lodges across the Ngozumpa glacier from Gokyo - the crossing takes about 2 hr. Mapped in OSM as Dragnag. Base for the Cho La.

waypoints.name: Cho La
waypoints.description: 5,368 m by OSM/SRTM, usually quoted as 5,420 m. Second pass. The east side is a small glacier with crevasses near the top - go early, on frozen snow, and rope up if unsure. The west descent is loose boulders.

waypoints.name: Dzongla
waypoints.description: ~4,830 m. Three or four lodges in a meadow under Cholatse and Taboche. Base for the Cho La from the east. Also spelled Zongla.

waypoints.name: Thukla Pass Memorials
waypoints.description: ~4,830 m. Ridge of stone chortens above Dughla remembering climbers and Sherpas lost on Everest, including Scott Fischer and Babu Chiri Sherpa.

waypoints.name: Lobuche
waypoints.description: 4,910 m. Cluster of lodges beside the Khumbu glacier moraine. Cold, busy and often crowded; book ahead in peak season.

waypoints.name: Gorak Shep
waypoints.description: 5,175 m. Highest lodges on the trek, on a sandy flat that was once a lake. Base for both Everest Base Camp and Kala Patthar. Sleep low if you can - many people feel rough here.

waypoints.name: Lobuche
waypoints.description: 4,910 m. Cluster of lodges beside the Khumbu glacier moraine. Cold, busy and often crowded; book ahead in peak season.

waypoints.name: Kongma La
waypoints.description: 5,535 m. Third and highest pass, and the hardest day of the circuit. From Lobuche you cross the Khumbu glacier first, then climb boulder slopes past frozen tarns. Little shelter and no water once you start.

waypoints.name: Chhukhung
waypoints.description: 4,730 m. Half a dozen lodges at the head of the Imja valley. Base for Chhukhung Ri, Island Peak and the east side of the Kongma La.

waypoints.name: Dingboche
waypoints.description: 4,410 m. Walled-field village in the Imja valley, with bakeries, wifi and the usual second acclimatisation stop. Nangkartshang (5,083 m) is the standard afternoon climb.

waypoints.name: Shomare
waypoints.description: 4,060 m. Small string of lodges between Pangboche and Dingboche; a good quiet alternative if the bigger villages are full.

waypoints.name: Pangboche
waypoints.description: 3,930 m. The oldest gompa in the Khumbu is in Upper Pangboche, a few minutes above the trail, with the finest Ama Dablam view on the route.

waypoints.name: Deboche
waypoints.description: 3,745 m. Quiet lodges in rhododendron forest below Tengboche, with a nunnery. Warmer and much less crowded than Tengboche itself.

waypoints.name: Tengboche
waypoints.description: 3,867 m. The Khumbu's principal monastery, on a ridge facing Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse and Ama Dablam. Afternoon puja is open to visitors. Mani Rimdu festival in October or November.

waypoints.name: Phunki Thanga
waypoints.description: 3,305 m. Water-driven prayer wheels and a couple of teahouses at the bridge. The 600 m climb to Tengboche starts here.

waypoints.name: Sanasa
waypoints.description: ~3,600 m. Trail junction: right for Tengboche and Everest Base Camp, left for Mong La, Dole and the Gokyo valley. A few tea stalls.

waypoints.name: Kyangjuma
waypoints.description: 3,610 m. Three or four lodges on the contouring trail east of Namche, with a superb Ama Dablam view.

waypoints.name: Khumjung
waypoints.description: 3,780 m. Big Sherpa village under Khumbila, with Hillary's school and the gompa that keeps the 'yeti scalp'. Best acclimatisation walk from Namche.

waypoints.name: Syangboche
waypoints.description: ~3,760 m. Dirt airstrip above Namche, now used mostly by helicopters. The standard Namche acclimatisation walk climbs past it.

waypoints.name: Namche Bazaar
waypoints.description: 3,440 m. The Khumbu's main town: banks, ATMs, bakeries, gear shops, hospital, wifi. Saturday market. Plan two nights here to acclimatise.

waypoints.name: Jorsalle
waypoints.description: ~2,795 m. Last lodges and last shop before the 600 m climb to Namche. The trail crosses the Hillary Bridge shortly after.

waypoints.name: Monjo
waypoints.description: 2,835 m. Sagarmatha National Park entrance is just beyond the village - permits and TIMS checked here. Good lodges.

waypoints.name: Phakding
waypoints.description: 2,610 m. Large lodge village on both banks of the Dudh Koshi; the standard first night out of Lukla.

waypoints.name: Ghat
waypoints.description: ~2,530 m. Also Nurning Ghat. Small village with lodges, a gompa and carved mani stones beside the Dudh Koshi.

waypoints.name: Chheplung
waypoints.description: 2,660 m. Where the Jiri and Lukla trails merge. Several lodges; mapped in OSM as Cheplung.

waypoints.name: Chaurikharka
waypoints.description: ~2,665 m. Village on the low trail between Surke and Chheplung, bypassing the climb to Lukla. Lodges, school and a gompa.

waypoints.name: Lukla
waypoints.description: 2,850 m. Tenzing-Hillary airport, dozens of lodges, ATMs, gear shops and the Sagarmatha National Park permit desk. Reached from Surke by a 550 m climb; most trekkers on the Jiri route only detour here to resupply.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Gokyo Ri
offTrailWaypoints.description: 5,357 m. 2-3 hr climb straight up from Gokyo. Arguably the best viewpoint in the Khumbu: Everest, Lhotse, Makalu, Cho Oyu and the whole Ngozumpa. Go at dawn.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Thonak Tsho (fourth lake)
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~4,870 m. South shore of the fourth Gokyo lake, about 1.5 hr north of Gokyo along the west side of the Ngozumpa. Easy acclimatisation walk; the fifth lake and Scoundrel's Viewpoint are another hour on.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Everest Base Camp
offTrailWaypoints.description: 5,364 m. On the Khumbu glacier below the Icefall. Tent city in April and May, bare moraine the rest of the year. Note the camp itself moves on the glacier each season; Everest is not visible from here.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Kala Patthar
offTrailWaypoints.description: 5,645 m. The classic Everest viewpoint - a rocky shoulder of Pumori, about 2 hr up from Gorak Shep. Sunrise is bitter; sunset is warmer and usually clearer.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Dughla
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~4,620 m. Two lodges at the foot of the Khumbu glacier terminal moraine. Standard lunch stop. Also spelled Thukla.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Chhukhung Ri
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~5,546 m. Steep 2-3 hr walk-up above the village, facing the Lhotse and Nuptse south faces and Ama Dablam's east side. Excellent acclimatisation.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Pheriche
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~4,270 m. Windy valley village with the Himalayan Rescue Association clinic - free altitude-sickness talks most afternoons in season.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Mong La
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~3,975 m. Chorten and two teahouses on the ridge above Sanasa, on the spur of Khumbila. The Gokyo valley trail drops steeply from here to Phortse Thanga.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Phortse Tenga
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~3,600 m (often quoted as 3,680 m). Two or three lodges at the river crossing below Mong La, where the trail from Phortse joins the Gokyo valley route. Also spelled Phortse Thanga.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Phortse
offTrailWaypoints.description: 3,800 m. Traditional village on a terrace above the Dudh Koshi, home to many climbing Sherpas and the Khumbu Climbing Center. Linked to Pangboche by a fine high traverse.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Dole
offTrailWaypoints.description: 4,050 m. Several lodges in a steep-sided valley; the usual first night on the Gokyo valley approach.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Luza
offTrailWaypoints.description: 4,360 m. Two lodges in a summer settlement between Dole and Machhermo.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Machhermo
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~4,390 m. Half a dozen lodges and an HRA aid post that runs a daily altitude talk. Site of a well-known 1974 yeti story.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Thodung
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~3,020 m. Yak-cheese factory and monastery on the ridge about 2 hr north of Deurali. Worthwhile detour if you have a spare half-day; there is simple accommodation.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Thubten Choling
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~3,060 m. Large Tibetan Buddhist monastery and nunnery about 1.5 hr up the valley from Junbesi, founded by refugees from Rongbuk in 1959. An easy half-day walk from a Junbesi rest day.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Hotel Everest View
offTrailWaypoints.description: 3,885 m. Terrace with the famous Everest and Ama Dablam view, an hour above Namche. Expensive tea, unbeatable outlook, and a perfect climb-high-sleep-low acclimatisation target.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Nangkartshang
offTrailWaypoints.description: 5,073 m. The standard acclimatisation climb from Dingboche, up the ridge north of the village. Prayer flags at the top and a wide view of Makalu, Ama Dablam and the Imja valley.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Khunde
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~3,840 m. Khumjung's twin village, five minutes further on and quieter again. Hillary's hospital is here. A better night than Namche: 400 m higher, a fraction of the beds, and the same walk back down in the morning.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Ngozumpa Tsho (fifth lake)
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~4,945 m by SRTM, usually quoted as 4,980 m. The fifth Gokyo lake. Scoundrel's Viewpoint is on the moraine five minutes east - Everest, Lhotse and Cho Oyu in one sweep, and almost nobody on it, an hour beyond a lake everyone stops at.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Ama Dablam Base Camp
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~4,600 m, approximate. Grassy meadow under the south-west face. Empty outside the autumn climbing season and a good acclimatisation walk from Pangboche that stays off the Base Camp trail entirely.

offTrailWaypoints.name: Lawudo Gompa
offTrailWaypoints.description: ~3,880 m. Retreat gompa and meditation cave on the shoulder above Thamo, about an hour up from the valley trail. Rarely visited.

waypoints.description: 3,780 m. Big Sherpa village under Khumbila, with Hillary's school and the gompa that keeps the 'yeti scalp'. Best acclimatisation walk from Namche.

waypoints.name: Syangboche
waypoints.description: ~3,760 m. Dirt airstrip above Namche, now used mostly by helicopters. The standard Namche acclimatisation walk climbs past it.

waypoints.name: Namche Bazaar
waypoints.description: 3,440 m. The Khumbu's main town: banks, ATMs, bakeries, gear shops, hospital, wifi. Saturday market. Plan two nights here to acclimatise.

waypoints.name: Dingboche
waypoints.description: 4,410 m. Walled-field village in the Imja valley, with bakeries, wifi and the usual second acclimatisation stop. Nangkartshang (5,083 m) is the standard afternoon climb.

waypoints.name: Nangkartshang
waypoints.description: 5,073 m. The standard acclimatisation climb from Dingboche, up the ridge north of the village. Prayer flags at the top and a wide view of Makalu, Ama Dablam and the Imja valley.

waypoints.name: Surke
waypoints.description: 2,300 m. Three or four lodges. Junction: left climbs steeply to Lukla, straight on stays low and joins the main trail at Chheplung.

waypoints.name: Lukla
waypoints.description: 2,850 m. Tenzing-Hillary airport, dozens of lodges, ATMs, gear shops and the Sagarmatha National Park permit desk. Reached from Surke by a 550 m climb; most trekkers on the Jiri route only detour here to resupply.
